scope.current_boundary: Teach that a constant-magnitude force perpendicular to the direction of motion causes centripetal acceleration, and that centripetal acceleration causes circular motion with constant angular speed. Do not teach the magnitude equations reserved for lesson 9702_t12_cm02_l04.
scope.previous_boundary_used: Angular speed and the relationships omega = 2 pi / T and v = r omega were treated only as prior knowledge. No earlier formula was re-taught or used for calculation.
scope.next_boundary_checked: Recall and use a = r omega squared, a = v squared / r, F = mr omega squared, and F = mv squared / r. Those equations and their numerical use are intentionally deferred.

question_patterns_used.name: Definition
question_patterns_used.lesson_response: Separated speed from velocity and supplied a clear, non-claimed-as-Cambridge term meaning for centripetal acceleration.

question_patterns_used.name: Explanation
question_patterns_used.lesson_response: Taught a causal route from inward resultant force to centripetal acceleration, changing velocity direction, circular path and constant angular speed.

question_patterns_used.lesson_response: Explained why calculation prompts use the inward acceleration, while deferring all magnitude equations to the next lesson.

questions_visited.why_selected: A direct, low-demand description of uniform circular motion tests the central distinction between constant speed and changing velocity.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: State constant speed or constant velocity magnitude and acceleration perpendicular to the velocity.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Recognise that changing direction changes velocity even when speed remains constant, then state the perpendicular acceleration direction.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Treating constant speed as constant velocity.
lesson_sections_informed: Why a sideways acceleration does not change the speed

questions_visited.why_selected: Directly asks what centripetal acceleration means and gives the required directional focus.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: State that the acceleration is perpendicular to the velocity.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Identify the instantaneous tangential velocity and the inward perpendicular acceleration.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Saying acceleration is in the direction of motion, or treating centripetal acceleration as an outward effect.
lesson_sections_informed: The three directions to keep separate
Why a sideways acceleration does not change the speed

questions_visited.why_selected: Uses a vertical loop to test the difference between an existing inward force and an additional inward contact force.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Explain why a car remaining in contact at the top of a loop needs centripetal acceleration greater than that supplied by weight alone.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Resolve the forces towards the centre and relate a larger required inward resultant to a contact force from the track.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Assuming gravity is always the only force involved in circular motion, or that a force is needed to balance the inward force.
lesson_sections_informed: The force that keeps the turn happening
A common confusion: constant magnitude is not constant direction

questions_visited.why_selected: Contrasts the direction of an inward resultant force with its very small magnitude in a slow circular motion.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Compare centripetal acceleration with free-fall acceleration and infer that the inward resultant force is negligible compared with weight.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Connect a small centripetal acceleration to a small inward resultant force, while keeping the force direction separate from its magnitude.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Thinking a force that has a changing direction must have a changing magnitude, or confusing resultant force with weight.
lesson_sections_informed: The force that keeps the turn happening
A common confusion: constant magnitude is not constant direction

questions_visited.why_selected: Requires a force-component explanation where a real force has both a vertical role and an inward centripetal role.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Explain why a spring extends more when a suspended sphere moves in a horizontal circle.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Identify the horizontal tension component as the inward force, the vertical component as balancing weight, and the resulting larger tension.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Calling the whole tension centripetal force without considering its vertical component.
lesson_sections_informed: The force that keeps the turn happening
Worked example: a ball on a string

questions_visited.why_selected: Tests several vector quantities that change in constant-speed circular motion.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Name two varying quantities, such as velocity, momentum, centripetal acceleration or resultant force.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Separate scalar speed from vectors whose directions change continuously.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Naming speed as varying, or overlooking that a vector varies when its direction changes.
